class.name: Material4D
class.description: Material4D is the base class for all 4D materials. It provides a way to color 4D meshes with help from its derived classes such as [WireMaterial4D] and [TetraMaterial4D]. Material4D can be set on a [Mesh4D] resource to define how the mesh should be colored, and/or overridden on a specific [MeshInstance4D] node.

method.name: _update_cross_section_material_3d
method.description: Callback for derived classes to update the 3D material used by the cross-section renderer. Do not call this method. This can be overridden by derived classes when creating a custom material type in GDScript or another scripting language.

method.name: _update_projected_material_3d
method.description: Callback for derived classes to update the 3D material used by the projected renderer. Do not call this method. This can be overridden by derived classes when creating a custom material type in GDScript or another scripting language.

method.name: append_albedo_color
method.description: Appends the given albedo color to the albedo color array of the material. This may be used to color various parts of the mesh, depending on the albedo source flags. Only used when any of the per-item color flags are set.

method.name: get_albedo_color
method.description: Gets the single albedo color of the material. Only used when the [constant COLOR_SOURCE_FLAG_SINGLE_COLOR] albedo source flag is set. If this flag is set together with any other flag, the single color acts as a modulate color.

method.name: get_albedo_color_array
method.description: Gets the albedo color array of the material. This may be used to color various parts of the mesh, depending on the albedo source flags. Only used when any of the per-item color flags are set.

method.name: get_albedo_color_of_edge
method.description: Gets the albedo color of the edge with the given index. The [param for_mesh] parameter is used to determine which mesh the edge belongs to. This function will cache the calculated edge colors, so it can be called multiple times without performance issues.

method.name: get_albedo_source_flags
method.description: Gets low-level flags that determine how the mesh is colored. This is meant to be used by the renderer to determine the appearance of colored objects. [b]Note:[/b] When making materials, use the high-level properties from the derived classes instead, such as [member WireMaterial4D.albedo_source] or [member TetraMaterial4D.albedo_source].

method.name: get_albedo_texture_map_offset
method.description: Gets the offset of the texture map (UV map or UVW map) applied to the base color or albedo 3D texture used for coloring the mesh. This is only used when any of the 3D texture flags are set in [member albedo_source_flags], and only when the texture transform mode is set to [constant TEXTURE_TRANSFORM_MODE_PER_CHANNEL]. This offset controls the texture map, not the texture itself. An offset of (0.25, 0.25, 0.25) will add this value to all texture coordinates, making a texture coordinate of zero start at a quarter of the way into the texture, which visually shifts the texture in the opposite direction of the offset. This is equivalent to Godot's [member BaseMaterial3D.uv1_offset] property, but is specific to the albedo material channel.

method.name: get_albedo_texture_map_scale
method.description: Gets the scale of the texture map (UV map or UVW map) applied to the base color or albedo 3D texture used for coloring the mesh. This is only used when any of the 3D texture flags are set in [member albedo_source_flags], and only when the texture transform mode is set to [constant TEXTURE_TRANSFORM_MODE_PER_CHANNEL]. This scale controls the texture map, not the texture itself. A scale of (2, 2, 2) will make the texture map cover the texture twice as many times on each axis, which has the effect of tiling the texture in a 2x2x2 pattern, making each visual copy of the texture appear half the size. This is equivalent to Godot's [member BaseMaterial3D.uv1_scale] property, but is specific to the albedo material channel.

method.name: get_cross_section_material_3d
method.description: Returns a 3D material to be used by the cross-section renderer. The returned material is automatically updated to match the properties of this material.

method.name: get_effective_albedo_texture_map_offset
method.description: Returns the effective offset of the texture map (UV map or UVW map) applied to the base color or albedo 3D texture used for coloring the mesh. This considers the texture transform mode (see [method get_texture_transform_mode]) and will read the appropriate offset value, or return zero if no offset is used. This value is only used when any of the 3D texture flags are set in [member albedo_source_flags].

method.name: get_effective_albedo_texture_map_scale
method.description: Returns the effective scale of the texture map (UV map or UVW map) applied to the base color or albedo 3D texture used for coloring the mesh. This considers the texture transform mode (see [method get_texture_transform_mode]) and will read the appropriate scale value, or return one if no scale is used. This value is only used when any of the 3D texture flags are set in [member albedo_source_flags].

method.name: get_projected_material_3d
method.description: Returns a 3D material to be used by the projected renderer. For material types that support projected rendering, the returned material is automatically updated to match the properties of this material. Unsupported material types return a material with no shader.

method.name: get_texture_map_offset
method.description: Gets the offset of the texture map (UV map or UVW map) applied to all material channels (albedo, emissive, normal, ORM, etc). This is only used when the texture transform mode is set to [constant TEXTURE_TRANSFORM_MODE_ALL_CHANNELS] and at least one channel uses a 3D texture. This offset controls the texture map, not the texture itself. An offset of (0.25, 0.25, 0.25) will add this value to all texture coordinates, making a texture coordinate of zero start at a quarter of the way into the texture, which visually shifts the texture in the opposite direction of the offset. This is equivalent to Godot's [member BaseMaterial3D.uv1_offset] property.

method.name: get_texture_map_scale
method.description: Gets the offset of the texture map (UV map or UVW map) applied to all material channels (albedo, emissive, normal, ORM, etc). This is only used when the texture transform mode is set to [constant TEXTURE_TRANSFORM_MODE_ALL_CHANNELS] and at least one channel uses a 3D texture. This scale controls the texture map, not the texture itself. A scale of (2, 2, 2) will make the texture map cover the texture twice as many times on each axis, which has the effect of tiling the texture in a 2x2x2 pattern, making each visual copy of the texture appear half the size. This is equivalent to Godot's [member BaseMaterial3D.uv1_scale] property.

method.name: get_texture_transform_mode
method.description: Gets the texture transform mode, which determines how the texture transform is applied to the various material channels. Texture transforms are only useful when the material uses 3D textures, such as when any of the 3D texture flags are set in [member albedo_source_flags]. See [enum TextureTransformMode] for options.

method.name: is_default_material
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this material is equivalent to the default material, meaning that its only color source is a single color, and that color is exactly white.

method.name: merge_with
method.description: Merges this material with another material. This will preserve color arrays if present, or create them as needed. For example, if merging the materials for a red single-color box and a blue single-color box, the resulting material will have a color array with reds at the start and blues at the end. The [param first_item_count] and [param second_item_count] parameters are used to determine how many items from each material should end up in the color array. These parameters should be set to the number of items of the meshes that use the materials. That may be edges, cells, or something else, depending on the albedo source flags. For [PolyMaterial4D], the items are always the polyhedral boundary cells colored by [member PolyMaterial4D.poly_albedo_color_array], so pass the cell counts of the meshes. Note that even if the item count numbers are set properly, the output color array may still be empty if color arrays are not necessary to color the mesh, such as if both input materials use the same single color. For example, merging materials for a red single-color box and a red single-color sphere will result in a red single-color material with no color arrays.

method.name: resize_albedo_color_array
method.description: Resize the albedo color array of the material, filling any new elements with the given color, or with white if no color is provided.

method.name: set_albedo_color
method.description: Sets the single albedo color of the material. Only used when the [constant COLOR_SOURCE_FLAG_SINGLE_COLOR] albedo source flag is set. If this flag is set together with any other flag, the single color acts as a modulate color.

method.name: set_albedo_color_array
method.description: Sets the color array of the material. This may be used to color various parts of the mesh, depending on the albedo source flags. Only used when any of the per-item color flags are set.

method.name: set_albedo_source_flags
method.description: Sets low-level flags that determine how the mesh is colored. This method can be used to implement a custom material type. [b]Note:[/b] When making materials, use the high-level properties from the derived classes instead, such as [member WireMaterial4D.albedo_source] or [member TetraMaterial4D.albedo_source].

method.name: set_albedo_texture_map_offset
method.description: Sets the offset of the texture map (UV map or UVW map) applied to the base color or albedo 3D texture used for coloring the mesh. This is only used when any of the 3D texture flags are set in [member albedo_source_flags], and only when the texture transform mode is set to [constant TEXTURE_TRANSFORM_MODE_PER_CHANNEL]. This offset controls the texture map, not the texture itself. This is equivalent to Godot's [member BaseMaterial3D.uv1_offset] property, but is specific to the albedo material channel.

method.description: Sets the scale of the texture map (UV map or UVW map) applied to the base color or albedo 3D texture used for coloring the mesh. This is only used when any of the 3D texture flags are set in [member albedo_source_flags], and only when the texture transform mode is set to [constant TEXTURE_TRANSFORM_MODE_PER_CHANNEL]. A scale of (2, 2, 2) will make the texture map cover the texture twice as many times on each axis, which has the effect of tiling the texture in a 2x2x2 pattern, making each visual copy of the texture appear half the size. This is equivalent to Godot's [member BaseMaterial3D.uv1_scale] property, but is specific to the albedo material channel.

method.description: Sets the offset of the texture map (UV map or UVW map) applied to all material channels (albedo, emissive, normal, ORM, etc). method.description: Sets the scale of the texture map (UV map or UVW map) applied to all material channels (albedo, emissive, normal, ORM, etc). This is only used when the texture transform mode is set to [constant TEXTURE_TRANSFORM_MODE_ALL_CHANNELS] and at least one channel uses a 3D texture. This scale controls the texture map, not the texture itself. A scale of (2, 2, 2) will make the texture map cover the texture twice as many times on each axis, which has the effect of tiling the texture in a 2x2x2 pattern, making each visual copy of the texture appear half the size. This is equivalent to Godot's [member BaseMaterial3D.uv1_scale] property.

method.name: set_texture_transform_mode
method.description: Sets the texture transform mode, which determines how the texture transform is applied to the various material channels. Texture transforms are only useful when the material uses 3D textures, such as when any of the 3D texture flags are set in [member albedo_source_flags]. See [enum TextureTransformMode] for options.

constants.constant: Flag to indicate that the color source is a single color. If this flag is set together with any other flag, the single color acts as a modulate color.
Flag to indicate that each item in the color array is used for a vertex.
Flag to indicate that each item in the color array is used for an edge.
Flag to indicate that each item in the color array is used for a face.
Flag to indicate that each item in the color array is used for a cell.
Flag to indicate that each vertex should be colored based on a 3D texture sampled by its UVW coordinates.
Flag to indicate that each edge should be colored based on a 3D texture sampled by the UVW coordinates of its two vertices.
Flag to indicate that each face should be colored based on a 3D texture sampled by the UVW coordinates of its three vertices.
Flag to indicate that each cell should be colored based on a 3D texture sampled by the UVW coordinates of its four vertices.
Flag to indicate that the mesh color should be sampled from a 4D texture directly mapped to the mesh's local space without using UVW coordinates.

Do not apply any texture transform to the texture coordinates. This is the default mode. Untransformed texture coordinates are useful for complex objects with dedicated materials and textures paired with the mesh, such as a character model whose face needs to remain on the head.
Apply the same texture transform to all material channels (albedo, emissive, normal, ORM, etc). Texture transforms are useful when applying generic textures to meshes.

Apply a different texture transform to each material channel (albedo, emissive, normal, ORM, etc). Per-channel texture transforms are useful when applying generic textures to meshes, and when the material channels do not need to align with each other, such as when scaling the albedo and normal textures for more detail while leaving the ORM texture unscaled to keep specific parts of the mesh shiny or rough. Prefer using [constant TEXTURE_TRANSFORM_MODE_ALL_CHANNELS] if the textures do not need to be transformed differently.
